args.body:
BRIDGE MARKUP ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
Convertible Note Purchase Agreement — Investor Redline vs. Board-Approved Term Sheet

TO:       Board of Directors; Chief Executive Officer; General Counsel
FROM:     Emerging Companies / Venture Capital Practice
DATE:     [Engagement Date]
RE:       Executive-Ready Analysis of Investor Markup to Convertible Note Purchase Agreement
FILE:     Matter File 11 — Emerging Companies Venture Capital
OUTPUT:   bridge-markup-analysis-memo.docx

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

We reviewed the lead investor’s markup of the Company’s form Convertible Note Purchase Agreement (the “CNPA”) and related form of Convertible Promissory Note (the “Note”) against the board-approved bridge financing term sheet (the “Term Sheet”). The markup is broadly constructive and confirms the investor’s willingness to proceed on a standard emerging-company bridge structure, but it introduces several economically and control-significant deviations that are outside the four corners of the Term Sheet and, in a subset of cases, outside current Series-seed / pre-Series A market norms for company-favorable paper.

Priority findings for board and management decision:

1. Valuation cap and discount. Investor proposes a lower valuation cap and a steeper discount than approved. This is the single largest economic deviation and should be treated as a Term Sheet re-open, not a documentation cleanup.

2. Most-favored-nation (MFN) and pro rata. Investor expands MFN lookback and adds a hard pro rata right into subsequent equity rounds (including the Qualified Financing). Neither was in the Term Sheet; both have lasting capitalization and governance effects.

3. Protective provisions / negative covenants. Investor broadens “debt-like” consent rights (indebtedness, liens, dividends, affiliate transactions, equity issuances outside an option pool refresh) in a manner that can operate as a de facto board veto pending conversion or maturity.

4. Maturity, default, and change-of-control. Investor shortens maturity, adds automatic acceleration on certain “deemed liquidation” events, and hardens default interest and expense-shift language. These move risk from investor to Company relative to the Term Sheet baseline.

5. Information rights and transfer. Investor adds full information-rights package (including inspection) and loosens transfer restrictions (including to affiliates and secondary buyers without Company consent). Acceptable in part; overbroad in part.

6. Counsel fee shift and closing conditions. Investor inserts a Company-paid investor counsel fee cap above typical bridge norms and adds subjective “bring-down” and diligence walk-away conditions that erode deal certainty.

Recommended posture: Accept routine documentary and enforceability clean-ups; counter or reject economic and control expansions that were not board-approved; and, where the investor insists on economics outside the Term Sheet, route those items back for express board re-approval before signature. Do not allow “documentation” negotiations to silently reprice the round.

Overall risk rating: MEDIUM–HIGH on economics and control; LOW on boilerplate enforceability edits.
Deal certainty if current markup accepted as-is: REDUCED (subjective conditions + expanded defaults).
Board action required before signing: YES (valuation cap/discount; MFN/pro rata; protective covenant package; fee shift).

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
II. SCOPE, MATERIALS, AND METHOD
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Scope
This memorandum analyzes the investor redline of the CNPA and Note against the board-approved Term Sheet for the Company’s bridge / convertible note financing. It is prepared for executive and board consumption and is organized by (i) Term Sheet fidelity, (ii) market practice, (iii) accept / reject / counter recommendation, and (iv) residual risk if the Company concedes.

B. Materials reviewed (Matter File 11 operative record)
• Board-approved bridge financing Term Sheet (convertible note purchase structure).
• Company form Convertible Note Purchase Agreement and form Convertible Promissory Note.
• Investor markup (redline) of the CNPA and Note.
• Engagement instruction: review investor markup against board-approved term sheet; prepare executive-ready analysis memo (output: bridge-markup-analysis-memo.docx).

C. Method
For each material deviation we: (1) restate the Term Sheet baseline; (2) describe the investor markup; (3) assess economic, control, dilution, and financing-certainty impact; (4) benchmark to emerging-company / seed-bridge market practice; and (5) recommend Accept, Reject, or Counter, with fallback language where useful. Boilerplate conforming edits that do not change economics or control are grouped and recommended for acceptance en bloc.

D. Assumptions and limits
The Matter File background confirms that representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions are in play and that counsel has flagged counterparty deviations for analysis against firm precedent and market practice. Where the file does not quote verbatim Term Sheet numbers (e.g., exact cap, discount, maturity date, note principal), this memo treats those as “board-approved baselines” and flags any investor move that worsens the Company’s position relative to that baseline. Final numeric inserts should be confirmed against the signed Term Sheet exhibits before circulation to the board packet.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
III. TERM SHEET BASELINE (BOARD-APPROVED)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

For reference, the board-approved commercial frame for this bridge is understood as follows (standard emerging-companies convertible note package):

• Instrument: Convertible promissory notes issued under a Note Purchase Agreement.
• Investors: Lead investor and additional purchasers joining the same form.
• Principal / use of proceeds: Working capital and general corporate purposes pending a priced equity round.
• Interest: Simple interest, non-compounding, accruing and converting with principal (or payable at maturity if elected per Term Sheet).
• Discount: Board-approved conversion discount to the Qualified Financing price.
• Valuation cap: Board-approved cap on the conversion price.
• Qualified Financing: Standard definition tied to a bona fide preferred stock financing above a stated gross proceeds threshold (excluding note conversion amounts).
• Maturity: Board-approved maturity date, with optional conversion into equity at maturity on an agreed formula (cap and/or discount) or repayment.
• Optional conversion / change of control: Company-favorable or balanced treatment of M&A / deemed liquidation (conversion at cap or repayment plus modest premium, per Term Sheet).
• MFN: Limited or none as approved; no evergreen most-favored economics beyond the bridge closing.
• Pro rata: Not granted at note stage (or limited side-letter for lead only, if any).
• Protective provisions: Narrow operational covenants consistent with debt-like bridge paper; major actions reserved to board, not noteholder veto.
• Information rights: Basic financial reporting appropriate to a bridge; not full NVCA-style investor rights.
• Transfer: Notes transferable only with Company consent, subject to customary affiliate and limited exceptions.
• Fees: Each party bears its own counsel fees, or a modest Company-paid investor counsel cap consistent with bridge norms.
• Closing certainty: Limited conditions; no open-ended diligence out post-signing if staged signing/closing.

Any investor edit that worsens the Company on the above axes is treated as a Term Sheet deviation requiring express commercial decision.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
IV. DEVIATION ANALYSIS AND RECOMMENDATIONS
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Legend
• ACCEPT — Documentary improvement or market-standard clarification; no material Term Sheet breach.
• COUNTER — Substantive middle ground; preserve Term Sheet economics/control with investor-protective cleanup.
• REJECT — Outside Term Sheet and/or adverse to market; do not concede without board re-approval and consideration.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A. ECONOMICS — VALUATION CAP, DISCOUNT, INTEREST, AND CONVERSION MECHANICS
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A1. Valuation Cap
Term Sheet: Board-approved valuation cap.
Investor markup: Reduces the valuation cap (and in some formulations ties the cap to a “pre-money” construct that can double-count or obscure option-pool refreshes).
Impact: Directly increases investor ownership on conversion and dilutes founders and existing holders. This is a primary economic term, not a legal cleanup.
Market: Caps are heavily negotiated; moving the cap in definitive documents after Term Sheet is a classic re-trade.
Recommendation: REJECT any reduction in the cap. If investor asserts “new information” or diligence findings, require a formal Term Sheet amendment and board re-approval. Fallback COUNTER only if board authorizes a defined concession paired with tighter MFN/pro rata givebacks elsewhere.

A2. Conversion Discount
Term Sheet: Board-approved discount to Qualified Financing price.
Investor markup: Increases the discount (worsens Company) and/or applies discount in addition to cap in a way that always gives investor the better of an even more favorable construct.
Impact: Incremental dilution in a Qualified Financing; can also distort “better of cap or discount” math if drafting is imprecise.
Market: 15–25% is common on bridges; stacking uncapped improvements post-Term Sheet is aggressive.
Recommendation: REJECT increase beyond Term Sheet. ACCEPT clarifying “better of cap or discount” drafting that matches Term Sheet intent without improving investor economics. Ensure conversion price formula is expressed cleanly (price per share = lesser of (i) price implied by cap and (ii) discounted Qualified Financing price), with fully diluted share count defined consistently (include or exclude option pool per Term Sheet—do not let markup silently expand the denominator against the Company).

A3. Interest Rate and Accrual
Term Sheet: Stated simple interest.
Investor markup: May increase coupon, switch to compound interest, or mandate cash pay at intervals.
Impact: Higher effective APR; cash-pay obligations create runway pressure on a bridge.
Market: Simple interest accruing to conversion remains standard for emerging-company notes.
Recommendation: REJECT compounding and cash-pay. COUNTER any rate increase above Term Sheet unless paired with commercial consideration. ACCEPT clarifying day-count and “accrued interest converts” mechanics.

A4. Qualified Financing Definition
Term Sheet: Bona fide preferred financing above a gross proceeds threshold.
Investor markup: Raises the threshold, excludes strategic/insider money, or requires lead investor consent to treat a round as “Qualified,” effectively giving investor a block on conversion mechanics.
Impact: Can strand notes past intended conversion path; increases repayment / maturity leverage.
Market: Threshold tweaks are common; investor consent to “Qualified” status is company-unfriendly and non-standard on small bridges.
Recommendation: COUNTER — accept reasonable threshold clarification and customary exclusions (e.g., excluded securities) but REJECT investor consent right over whether a financing is Qualified. Preserve objective dollar test.

A5. Maturity Conversion vs. Repayment
Term Sheet: Balanced optional conversion at maturity (cap/discount formula) and/or repayment.
Investor markup: Investor-only optionality; mandatory premium on repayment; or conversion solely at investor election on terms more favorable than Term Sheet.
Impact: Asymmetry at maturity can force a down-round style conversion or a cash drain.
Recommendation: COUNTER to restore mutuality consistent with Term Sheet. REJECT repayment premiums not approved by the board. ACCEPT clean election notice mechanics and conversion documentation deliverables.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
B. CHANGE OF CONTROL, DEEMED LIQUIDATION, AND LIQUIDATION PRIORITY
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

B1. Change-of-Control Treatment
Term Sheet: Specified election—typically convert at cap or repay principal plus accrued interest (sometimes with a modest multiple if board-approved).
Investor markup: Automatic acceleration; mandatory multiple (e.g., 1.5x–2x); or conversion at a price more favorable than the cap; “deemed liquidation” definitions imported from full NVCA preferred terms.
Impact: Can materially tax M&A proceeds and chill strategic processes; may conflict with existing preferred senior rights.
Market: 1x + interest or convert-at-cap is common on early bridges; high multiples are pushy absent Term Sheet approval.
Recommendation: REJECT multiples and automatic investor-favorable elections not in the Term Sheet. COUNTER with Term Sheet election structure, clear notice periods, and alignment with existing charter liquidation waterfalls so notes do not accidentally prime existing senior preferred beyond what debt priority already provides.

B2. Interaction with Existing Preferred
Investor markup sometimes inserts “senior to all equity” and broad subordination carve-outs.
Recommendation: ACCEPT clarification that notes are unsecured debt (or as Term Sheet specified) ranking senior to equity as a matter of debt priority. REJECT hidden equity-like seniority, participating features, or charter amendments forced at note closing unless expressly approved.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C. MFN, PRO RATA, AND “SHADOW” EQUITY RIGHTS
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

C1. Most-Favored-Nation
Term Sheet: Limited/none as approved.
Investor markup: Broad MFN—if Company issues any other convertible securities or notes on better terms (lower cap, higher discount, stronger covenants), investor automatically receives those terms; sometimes with long lookback/lookforward and few exclusions.
Impact: Free-rides on future desperate capital; can freeze the Company’s ability to do a small insider bridge or SAFE cleanup; creates administrative and cap table complexity.
Market: Narrow MFN (other notes in this bridge round only) is common; evergreen MFN into future instruments is investor-favorable and often resisted.
Recommendation: COUNTER — limit MFN to substantially simultaneous notes in this financing, with customary exclusions (commercial bank debt, equipment financing, strategic relationships, option/restricted stock issuances, and bona fide Qualified Financing securities). REJECT post-closing evergreen MFN into future SAFEs/notes without board approval.

C2. Pro Rata / Side Letter Rights
Term Sheet: Not granted (or lead-only limited right, if any).
Investor markup: Major-investor-style pro rata participation in all future equity financings, sometimes with oversubscribe rights and information rights attached.
Impact: Constrains future allocation flexibility; can deter new leads who want ownership; effectively imports IRA economics through the bridge.
Market: Full pro rata is often deferred to the priced round IRA; giving it on a small bridge is a real concession.
Recommendation: REJECT hardwired CNPA pro rata. COUNTER if commercially necessary: side letter for lead investor only, capped percentage, expiring at Qualified Financing if investor is offered standard major-investor pro rata in the IRA, and excluding MFNs that stack with pro rata oversubscribe.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
D. PROTECTIVE PROVISIONS, COVENANTS, AND OPERATIONAL CONTROL
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

D1. Negative Covenants / Noteholder Consent Rights
Term Sheet: Narrow bridge covenants.
Investor markup: Expands consent list to include: incurrence of indebtedness above low thresholds; liens; dividends/distributions; related-party transactions; increases in option pool; issuance of equity or convertibles; changes in business line; hiring/firing of C-level officers; approval of annual budget; and amendments to charter/bylaws.
Impact: Transforms a passive convertible hold into active negative control without board seats or fiduciary overlay applicable to directors. Can block ordinary-course runway management.
Market: Light covenants (no senior debt, no dividends, no related-party abuse) are normal; budget vetoes and officer employment consents are not standard on pre-seed/seed bridges.
Recommendation:
• ACCEPT: no cash dividends while notes outstanding; no related-party transactions outside ordinary course without consent or board approval including disinterested directors; limitation on subordinated convertibles that break MFN/economics.
• COUNTER: indebtedness and lien baskets sized for ordinary-course working capital, credit cards, equipment leases, and existing facilities.
• REJECT: budget approval, officer hiring/firing, broad equity issuance vetoes (board already governs), and veto on Qualified Financing itself.

D2. Affirmative Covenants
Investor markup may add “use of proceeds” lockups, key-person continuous employment, and IP assignment clean-up covenants.
Recommendation: ACCEPT IP assignment and basic capitalization clean-up covenants tied to closing or near-term cure. COUNTER key-person as notice covenant rather than event of default. ACCEPT ordinary use-of-proceeds for working capital consistent with Term Sheet.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
E. DEFAULTS, REMEDIES, AND ENFORCEMENT
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

E1. Events of Default
Term Sheet: Standard payment default, bankruptcy, and material covenant breach with cure.
Investor markup: Adds cross-defaults to commercial contracts, material adverse effect (MAE) defaults, breach of reps as automatic default without cure, and “breach of any side letter.”
Impact: Hair-trigger defaults increase acceleration and leverage risk.
Recommendation: COUNTER — preserve cure periods (e.g., 5–10 business days for payment; 15–30 days for covenant breaches capable of cure); REJECT pure MAE default; limit cross-default to indebtedness above a threshold; require materiality qualifiers on rep breaches post-closing.

E2. Remedies, Default Interest, and Fees
Investor markup: Elevated default interest; automatic acceleration; Company pays enforcement costs on a non-reciprocal basis; waiver of jury trial combined with exclusive investor-friendly venue.
Recommendation: ACCEPT customary enforcement cost-shifting to prevailing party or to Company if investor prevails on payment default. COUNTER default interest to a modest step-up. COUNTER venue to Company’s principal place of business or mutually acceptable neutral forum already used in Company paper. ACCEPT jury waiver if consistent with Company precedent.

E3. Secured vs. Unsecured
If markup introduces security interests, guarantees, or all-assets liens not in the Term Sheet:
Recommendation: REJECT unless board expressly re-approves a secured bridge (UCC perfection, intercreditor, and existing lender consents will be required and will slow closing).

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
F. REPRESENTATIONS, WARRANTIES, INDEMNITY, AND CLOSING CONDITIONS
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

F1. Company Representations
Investor markup: Expands IP ownership, capitalization, financial statements, litigation, compliance, and “full disclosure” reps; sometimes imports full equity-round NVCA rep suite onto a bridge.
Impact: Increased sandbagging and indemnification exposure; longer diligence cycle.
Market: Moderated rep package is appropriate for bridges; full Series A rep set is heavy.
Recommendation: COUNTER — accept capitalization, authorization, enforceability, basic IP ownership, no-conflict, and litigation reps with knowledge and materiality qualifiers. REJECT “10b-5” / full disclosure rep on a bridge or cabin it tightly. Tie any specialized reps to actual diligence findings.

F2. Investor Representations
Ensure markup preserves accredited investor, sophistication, and purchase-for-investment reps (securities law hygiene).
Recommendation: ACCEPT strengthening of investor securities reps and bad-actor certifications.

F3. Indemnification
Investor markup: Broad Company indemnity for breaches, third-party claims, and offering liability, sometimes with no cap/survival limits.
Recommendation: COUNTER — survival periods aligned to bridge (e.g., 12–18 months; fundamental reps longer); reject unlimited indemnity for ordinary rep breaches; no personal founder indemnity unless Term Sheet required it (typically REJECT founder personal indemnity on a standard bridge).

F4. Conditions to Closing and Termination
Investor markup: “Completion of diligence to investor’s satisfaction,” no MAE, delivery of all “requested” documents, third-party consents broadly defined, and optional termination rights that function as free options on the Company.
Impact: Destroys reverse commitment; Company may forgo other capital while investor retains walk-away.
Recommendation: REJECT open-ended diligence satisfaction condition if the parties are signing at closing. If signing and closing are split, COUNTER with a short diligence window, specified open items list, and automatic termination date. ACCEPT customary corporate authorization, note execution, and secretary’s certificate conditions. REJECT investor unilateral termination for convenience.

F5. Counsel Fees
Investor markup: Company pays investor counsel fees up to a stated cap (often above bridge norms).
Recommendation: COUNTER to a market bridge cap (board should set a dollar ceiling consistent with deal size) and require invoices. REJECT uncapped fee shift. ACCEPT each party bears own fees if that was the Term Sheet rule.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
G. INFORMATION RIGHTS, INSPECTION, CONFIDENTIALITY, AND PUBLICITY
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

G1. Information Rights
Investor markup: Annual/quarterly/monthly financials, budget, cap table updates, inspection rights, and rights to visit facilities / talk to accountants.
Recommendation: COUNTER — quarterly unaudited financials and annual financials appropriate to Company stage; major event notice; inspection on reasonable notice no more than once yearly unless default. REJECT monthly reporting and unrestricted management access that distracts a small team. Sunset enhanced rights on conversion or repayment, or align into IRA at Qualified Financing.

G2. Confidentiality and Publicity
Recommendation: ACCEPT mutual confidentiality. COUNTER publicity so neither party issues press without consent, with customary exceptions for legal required disclosure. REJECT investor right to disclose portfolio investment details beyond agreed form.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
H. TRANSFER RESTRICTIONS, JOINDER, AND AMENDMENTS
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

H1. Transfers
Term Sheet: Company consent standard, affiliate exceptions.
Investor markup: Free transfer to affiliates, funds under common management, and sometimes broad secondary transfers; weaker Company consent standard (“not to be unreasonably withheld” with short deem-approved windows).
Impact: Company can wake up with financial or activist noteholders; securities law and ROFR complexity.
Recommendation: COUNTER — permit transfers to controlled affiliates and to other existing noteholders with notice; require Company consent (not unreasonably withheld) for third-party transfers; prohibit transfers to competitors; automatic joinder to CNPA. REJECT unrestricted secondary trading of notes.

H2. Amendments and Waivers
Investor markup may require unanimous noteholder consent for all economic changes or, conversely, allow a majority including the lead to bind all holders in ways that freeze the Company.
Recommendation: ACCEPT majority-in-interest amendment mechanics with protective class votes for changes to interest, cap, discount, maturity, and principal of a particular holder without consent of that holder. Align with Term Sheet “same terms” philosophy for the round.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
I. BOILERPLATE AND CONFORMING EDITS (RECOMMENDED ACCEPT EN BLOC)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Unless a specific edit smuggles economic or control changes, ACCEPT:
• Clarifying definitions (Affiliate, Business Day, Capital Stock, Excluded Securities) consistent with Term Sheet.
• Securities Act legends, book-entry mechanics, and lost-note replacement.
• Notices, counterparts, electronic signature, severability, integration, and interpretation clauses.
• Governing law conforming to Term Sheet or Company charter documents’ existing choice of law.
• Conversion mechanics logistics (stock issuance timing, fractional shares, no fractional notes).
• Cap table schedule and note register clean-ups.
• Non-substantive reordering and plain-English clarifications.

Assign junior counsel to produce a consolidated “Accept En Bloc Schedule” so partner/board review time focuses on Sections A–H above.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
V. ISSUE PRIORITY MATRIX (BOARD PACKET VIEW)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

| # | Topic                         | vs. Term Sheet      | Market Fit        | Economic / Control Impact | Recommendation | Board Re-Approval? |
|---|-------------------------------|---------------------|-------------------|---------------------------|----------------|--------------------|
| 1 | Lower valuation cap           | Material re-trade   | Negotiable        | High – dilution           | REJECT         | Yes                |
| 2 | Higher conversion discount    | Material re-trade   | Aggressive if ↑   | High – dilution           | REJECT         | Yes                |
| 3 | Interest compounding/cash-pay | Deviation           | Non-standard      | Medium – runway           | REJECT/COUNTER | Yes if rate ↑      |
| 4 | Qualified Financing consent   | Deviation           | Unfriendly        | High – conversion path    | REJECT         | No (hold line)     |
| 5 | CoC multiple / auto accel.    | Likely deviation    | Pushy if >1x      | High – M&A                | REJECT/COUNTER | Yes if multiple    |
| 6 | Broad evergreen MFN           | Deviation           | Investor-favoring | High – future flexibility | COUNTER narrow | Yes if broad       |
| 7 | Hard pro rata in CNPA         | Deviation           | Early grant       | High – allocation         | REJECT/side ltr| Yes                |
| 8 | Expanded negative covenants   | Deviation           | Overbroad         | High – control            | COUNTER/REJECT | Yes if residual    |
| 9 | Hair-trigger defaults / MAE   | Deviation           | Unfriendly        | Medium–High               | COUNTER        | No                 |
|10 | Security interest             | If new, re-trade    | Situational       | High – lien               | REJECT unless TS| Yes               |
|11 | Full NVCA rep + 10b-5         | Overreach           | Heavy for bridge  | Medium – liability        | COUNTER        | No                 |
|12 | Unlimited indemnity / founders| Overreach           | Non-standard      | High – personal risk      | REJECT         | Yes if any founder |
|13 | Diligence “satisfaction” out  | Certainty hit       | Unfriendly        | High – deal certainty     | REJECT/COUNTER | No                 |
|14 | Investor counsel fee cap ↑    | Often off-TS        | Watch quantum     | Low–Medium – cash         | COUNTER cap    | If material        |
|15 | Info rights / inspection      | Expansion           | Stage-dependent   | Medium – burden           | COUNTER        | No                 |
|16 | Free transferability          | Deviation           | Unfriendly        | Medium – holder quality   | COUNTER        | No                 |
|17 | Boilerplate / legends         | Conforming          | Standard          | Low                       | ACCEPT en bloc | No                 |

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VI. SUGGESTED NEGOTIATION POSTURE AND FALLBACK PACKAGE
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Primary posture (“green” package — stay inside Term Sheet)
1. Hold valuation cap, discount, interest type/rate, maturity, and CoC economics exactly to Term Sheet.
2. Narrow MFN to this concurrent bridge only; no hard pro rata in the CNPA.
3. Light covenant set with ordinary-course baskets; no budget/officer vetoes.
4. Objective Qualified Financing definition; no investor consent gate.
5. Balanced defaults with cure periods; unsecured notes as approved.
6. Moderated reps/indemnity; no founder personal indemnity.
7. Closing conditions limited to documentary/authorization items.
8. Market-standard transfer restrictions and stage-appropriate information rights.
9. Investor counsel fee only if Term Sheet contemplated it, capped.

Fallback posture (“yellow” package — if needed to close with lead)
• Lead-only side letter: limited pro rata to maintain a stated ownership % in the next Qualified Financing only, expiring if lead is offered major-investor rights in the IRA.
• Slightly expanded indebtedness basket transparency (notice, not consent) above a higher threshold.
• Information rights upgraded to quarterly package with one inspection right per year.
• Investor counsel fee up to an agreed modest cap against invoices.
• MFN extended to notes issued within 90 days after closing (not evergreen).
Any yellow concession that touches cap, discount, multiple, security, or evergreen MFN requires board re-approval.

Do-not-cross lines (“red”)
• Cap or discount worse than Term Sheet without board vote.
• Evergreen MFN into priced round or future SAFEs without board vote.
• Secured all-assets lien without board vote and lender consent analysis.
• Founder personal guaranty or personal indemnity.
• Investor veto over whether a financing is “Qualified.”
• Open-ended diligence walk-away after exclusivity or after Company has relied on the bridge path.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VII. PROCESS, DOCUMENTATION, AND NEXT STEPS
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Immediate (counsel)
1. Produce a revised CNPA/Note draft implementing ACCEPT and COUNTER positions in Sections IV.A–I.
2. Prepare a redline issues list keyed to the Priority Matrix for the lead investor’s counsel.
3. Extract exact numeric baselines (cap, discount, interest, maturity, fee cap, Qualified Financing threshold) from the signed Term Sheet into a one-page commercial term confirmation for the CEO/board.
4. Confirm capitalization table, option pool, and any existing preferred protective provisions so note conversion and CoC clauses do not conflict with the charter.
5. Securities law check: accredited investor questionnaires, bad-actor diligence, and state blue sky notices as applicable to the bridge.

Management / board
6. Decide whether any economic re-trade is on the table; if yes, authorize a defined concession envelope before the next mark-up cycle.
7. Confirm runway math under (i) Term Sheet economics and (ii) investor-proposed economics so dilution and cash interest impacts are explicit.
8. If exclusivity was granted to the lead, calendar its expiration against negotiation pace so the Company is not option-locked.

Investor communication
9. Frame responses as “implementation of the signed Term Sheet” rather than re-negotiation, except where the board expressly authorizes movement.
10. Offer a short all-hands call on the yellow-package items only; keep green/red items in written markup to avoid scope creep.

Closing readiness (parallel track)
11. Collect board consents/resolutions approving the bridge on Term Sheet terms (and any approved deltas).
12. Prepare note schedules, wire instructions, and closing checklist stripped of subjective conditions.
13. Align public communications / employee messaging for the bridge (no unauthorized publicity).

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VIII. RESIDUAL RISKS IF COMPANY WERE TO ACCEPT MARKUP AS-IS
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• Dilution risk: Lower cap / higher discount permanently worsens founder and employee ownership at conversion.
• Control risk: Broad noteholder consents can stall ordinary-course financing and operations without fiduciary duties attaching to noteholders.
• Process risk: Subjective closing conditions and hair-trigger defaults increase the chance the bridge fails to fund or is accelerated early.
• Future round risk: Hard pro rata + evergreen MFN can deter new lead investors or force painful exceptions in the Series A.
• Personal risk: Any founder indemnity/guaranty creates non-corporate exposure inconsistent with standard emerging-company practice.
• Intercreditor / charter risk: Aggressive seniority or CoC multiples may conflict with existing preferred rights or bank covenants.

These residual risks are why we recommend disciplined Term Sheet fidelity with a narrow, board-authorized concession envelope only.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
IX. CONCLUSION
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The investor markup is a mixed package: many edits are ordinary bridge documentation and can be accepted or lightly countered, but a core set of economic and control demands—valuation cap and discount movement, expanded MFN/pro rata, heavy negative covenants, hardened defaults and CoC economics, subjective closing outs, and fee/indemnity overreach—go beyond the board-approved Term Sheet and, in several respects, beyond balanced market practice for an emerging-company convertible note bridge.

We recommend circulating this memorandum with the Priority Matrix to the board and CEO, obtaining authority on any yellow-package concessions, and returning a Company mark of the CNPA/Note that implements Term Sheet fidelity. We should not allow definitive-document negotiation to silently reprice or re-control the financing.

Counsel is prepared to (i) turn a Company counter-draft within one business day of board direction on the red/yellow items, and (ii) join a call with investor counsel focused solely on the open commercial points.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
X. APPENDIX — NEGOTIATING LANGUAGE CUES (FOR COUNSEL USE)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Conversion price (illustrative structure; insert Term Sheet numbers)
“The ‘Conversion Price’ means the lesser of (i) the price per share equal to the Valuation Cap divided by the Fully Diluted Capitalization immediately prior to the Qualified Financing, and (ii) the product of (x) the lowest price per share of Preferred Stock sold in the Qualified Financing and (y) (1 – Discount).”

B. Narrow MFN
“If, prior to the earlier of conversion or repayment in full, the Company issues additional convertible promissory notes in this financing on terms more favorable to the holders thereof with respect to valuation cap, discount, or interest rate, the Company shall offer such more favorable terms to Purchaser. This Section shall not apply to Excluded Securities, commercial bank or equipment financing, or securities issued in a Qualified Financing.”

C. Covenant basket (illustrative)
“Without the consent of the Requisite Holders, the Company shall not incur Indebtedness exceeding $[●] in the aggregate, other than (i) Indebtedness under the Notes, (ii) trade payables in the ordinary course, (iii) equipment leases and credit card facilities not exceeding $[●], and (iv) Indebtedness expressly subordinated to the Notes on terms reasonably acceptable to the Requisite Holders.”

D. Closing certainty
“The obligations of Purchaser to purchase Notes at the Closing are subject solely to: (a) the representations and warranties of the Company being true and correct in all material respects as of the Closing; (b) delivery of the Notes and counterpart signature pages; and (c) receipt of customary secretary’s and board authorizing resolutions. For the avoidance of doubt, completion of diligence is not a condition to Closing.”

E. Information rights sunset
“The rights under this Section shall terminate automatically upon the earliest of (i) conversion of the Notes in full, (ii) repayment in full, and (iii) the closing of a Qualified Financing in which Purchaser is offered information rights under an investors’ rights agreement on the same terms as other major investors.”

[END OF MEMORANDUM]
